To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sphericity and/or thrust distributions can be used to distinguish the ADD and the MSSM production scenarios of a charged leptons pair with large missing energy.

the event shape variables sphericity and/or thrust are able to distinguish between the MSSM and ADD models of new physics for the parameter ranges where the cross-sections for the two models are comparable.

1) For the ADD scenario, the event shape distribution for the production of a lepton pair plus a large missing energy is very similar to that for the production of two photons, and 2) For the MSSM scenario, the event is more spherical than for ADD, and the distribution of the sphericity variable S has a sharp cutoff at 1.0, while for ADD it does not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the production of a charged leptons with a large missing transverse momentum in the context of the MSSM and ADD scenarios.
the physics of extra dimensions and supersymmetry at the linear collider.
the physics of the Higgs boson and the physics of the top quark.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, if a linear collider experiment were to observe a l+l-+Emiss event with a cross-section of 10 pb or more, then the MSSM scenario would be excluded, and that, if the cross-section is below 10 pb, then the ADD scenario would be excluded.

for the parameter ranges studied, a linear collider with an initial center-of-mass energy of 500 GeV and a luminosity of 100 fb−1 is capable of discriminating between the ADD and MSSM scenarios for the production of a lepton pair with a large transverse missing energy.
for the parameter space considered in this paper, the ADD scenario is clearly distinguishable from the MSSM scenario by using event shapes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ADD scenario can be excluded at a 95% confidence level for a center-of-mass energy of 1 TeV and integrated luminosity of 50 fb-1, while for the MSSM scenario the exclusion limit is 2.2 TeV for an integrated luminosity of only 10 fb-1.
, for a given integrated luminosity, a linear collider is able to discriminate between the two scenarios with a higher degree of confidence than a hadron collider.

, in the region of phase space that is accessible at the ILC (i.e. the region with a small missing transverse momentum), the ADD model is clearly distinguishable from the MSSM, and that, in the high energy region, the ADD model is distinguishable from the minimal supersymmetrical standard model (MSSM).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sphericity variable is a very powerful tool to distinguish the ADD model from the MSSM, especially for low values of the center of mass energy.
, while it is not possible to distinguish between these two models in terms of total cross-sections, event shape variables provide an effective means of discriminating between them.
a linear collider can provide an excellent means for distinguishing the MSSM from the ADD scenario, and that event shape analyses can play a key role in this regard.
